title: Neovim as an IDE
goal: Syntax trees, a language server, completion, commenting and surround: IDE features, driven by vim grammar.

lessons.title: Treesitter: the editor understands your code

concepts.desc: turn on treesitter highlighting for the buffer. Lua, Markdown and help files get it automatically. Other languages need a FileType autocmd.
show the syntax tree of the buffer. Move in it and the source cursor follows.
select the parent syntax node (repeat an to grow) / a child node (in to shrink).
fold by syntax: functions, blocks, objects.
close / open / toggle a fold; open all / close all.
show the highlight groups and treesitter captures under the cursor.

lessons.tip: `van` pressed again and again is the fastest way to select "this argument, this call, this statement, this function" without counting brackets.

quiz.q: Which command shows the syntax tree of the current buffer?
In visual mode, which keys expand the selection to the parent syntax node?
quiz.a: an (repeat to keep growing); in shrinks to a child node.

quiz.q: How do you enable treesitter highlighting for C files?
quiz.a: A FileType autocmd for 'c' that calls vim.treesitter.start()

quiz.q: Which foldexpr gives syntax-aware folding?
Toggle the fold under the cursor; open all folds.
Which parsers ship with Neovim 0.12 itself?
quiz.a: c, lua, vim, vimdoc, query, markdown, markdown_inline. Others (TypeScript, Python, ...) come from nvim-treesitter.

lessons.title: LSP: plug in a language server

concepts.desc: a server config file that returns { cmd, filetypes, root_markers, settings }.
define or extend a server config from init.lua (merged with lsp/<name>.lua).
start the server automatically for matching filetypes.
files that mark the project root (tsconfig.json, package.json, .git).
see enabled configs, attached clients and their log file.
plugin that ships ready-made lsp/*.lua configs for hundreds of servers.

lessons.tip: Learn it once without plugins: a 4-line lsp/tsc.lua plus vim.lsp.enable('tsc') is the whole setup. TypeScript 7's compiler is its own language server (tsc --lsp --stdio). nvim-lspconfig just saves you writing those files.

quiz.q: Which function turns on a configured server for future buffers?
What does an lsp/<name>.lua file return?
quiz.a: A table with the config: cmd, filetypes, root_markers and optionally settings.

quiz.q: What is `root_markers` for?
quiz.a: To find the project root by looking upward for those files; the server starts with that root as its workspace.

quiz.q: How do you check whether a server is attached to the current buffer?
TypeScript 7: what command starts its built-in language server?
What does nvim-lspconfig give you in Neovim 0.11+?
quiz.a: Ready-made lsp/<name>.lua configs; you still call vim.lsp.enable().

lessons.title: LSP keys: navigate and refactor

concepts.desc: hover documentation / type of the symbol under the cursor.
go to definition (through LSP tagfunc) / jump back.
rename / code action / references / implementation / type definition.
list the document's symbols (outline).
next / previous / last / first diagnostic.
show the diagnostic under the cursor in a floating window.
signature help while typing arguments.

lessons.tip: Ctrl-] to dive into a definition, Ctrl-o to come back: it's the jump list you learned in week 6, now crossing files. Rename (grn) from the definition: at an import site the server may just add an alias.

quiz.q: Rename the symbol under the cursor across the project.
List all references to the symbol under the cursor.
quiz.a: grr (results go to the quickfix list).

quiz.q: Jump to the next diagnostic, then show its full message.
Show hover docs for the symbol under the cursor.
Open code actions (e.g. add missing import).
You jumped to a definition with Ctrl-]. How do you go back?
quiz.a: Ctrl-o (or Ctrl-t from the tag stack).

lessons.title: Completion, commenting and surround

concepts.desc: built-in LSP completion, turned on in an LspAttach autocmd.
next / previous item, accept, cancel the completion menu.
trigger omni (LSP) completion manually.
toggle comments on a line / a motion (gcip, gc3j) / a selection. Built in.
nvim-surround: add surroundings. ysiw" quotes a word, yss) wraps the line.
gc is also a text object for a block of commented lines: gcgc uncomments the block, dgc deletes it.
nvim-surround: change cs"' / delete ds( surroundings.

lessons.tip: gc is an operator like d or y, so text objects work: gcip comments a paragraph, gcap includes the blank line, and . repeats it.

quiz.q: Comment out the current paragraph.
Accept the selected completion item (built-in menu).
nvim-surround: change surrounding double quotes to single quotes.
nvim-surround: wrap the word under the cursor in parentheses.
quiz.a: ysiw) (or ysiw( for padding with spaces)

quiz.q: nvim-surround: delete the surrounding brackets [ ].
Where do you call vim.lsp.completion.enable, and why there?
quiz.a: In an LspAttach autocmd: it needs the client id and buffer of the server that just attached.

lessons.title: Week 11 review

concepts.desc: toggle comment on a line / paragraph (uses 'commentstring', e.g. -- %s for Lua).
hover, definition, rename, action, references.
diagnostics
syntax-tree selection
surround

lessons.tip: The IDE features are operators and motions too: gc takes text objects, grr fills the quickfix list you navigate with :cn.

quiz.q: Comment the current line and the 2 lines below it.
Which option decides what comment marker gc uses?
Show the type signature while typing function arguments in insert mode.
Go to the first diagnostic in the buffer.
Show the document outline (symbols).
Select the whole enclosing function call with treesitter, starting from an argument.
quiz.a: v then an (repeat an until the call is selected).
